mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 2% at the time of trigger).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market remains strong (PAYEMS YoY growth > 1%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising commodity prices (HOUST > 10% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present when labor market is overheating (UNRATE < 3.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in personal savings (RSAFS YoY growth > 8%) combined with a decline in consumer spending (GDPC1 YoY growth < 1%) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising household credit growth.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months) signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation risk, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate rate hikes and strong corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rising unemployment (UNRATE > 6%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates a weakening residential construction sector, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong mortgage credit growth.
